# HELP go_cpu_classes_gc_pause_cpu_seconds_total Estimated total CPU time spent with the application paused by the GC. Even if only one thread is running during the pause, this is computed as GOMAXPROCS times the pause latency because nothing else can be executing. This is the exact sum of samples in /sched/pauses/total/gc:seconds if each sample is multiplied by GOMAXPROCS at the time it is taken. This metric is an overestimate, and not directly comparable to system CPU time measurements. Compare only with other /cpu/classes metrics. Sourced from /cpu/classes/gc/pause:cpu-seconds.
# TYPE go_cpu_classes_gc_pause_cpu_seconds_total counter
go_cpu_classes_gc_pause_cpu_seconds_total 0.003020735

# HELP go_gc_limiter_last_enabled_gc_cycle GC cycle the last time the GC CPU limiter was enabled. This metric is useful for diagnosing the root cause of an out-of-memory error, because the limiter trades memory for CPU time when the GC's CPU time gets too high. This is most likely to occur with use of SetMemoryLimit. The first GC cycle is cycle 1, so a value of 0 indicates that it was never enabled. Sourced from /gc/limiter/last-enabled:gc-cycle.
# TYPE go_gc_limiter_last_enabled_gc_cycle gauge
go_gc_limiter_last_enabled_gc_cycle 0

# HELP kueue_workload_eviction_latency_seconds The time from workload eviction (WorkloadEvicted condition becomes True) until the workload returns to Pending (quota released).\nObserved on status transition from admitted or quota-reserved to pending while WorkloadEvicted remains True.\nEach matching update observes one latency sample (seconds) into this histogram; Prometheus aggregates samples across workloads.\nUses the eviction condition LastTransitionTime on the updated object as the start time; cluster_queue is taken from status.admission.cluster_queue on the pre-update object when set and non-empty (otherwise no sample is recorded for that update).\nThe label 'reason' can have the following values:\n- "Preempted" means that the workload was evicted in order to free resources for a workload with a higher priority or reclamation of nominal quota.\n- "PodsReadyTimeout" means that the eviction took place due to a PodsReady timeout.\n- "AdmissionCheck" means that the workload was evicted because at least one admission check transitioned to False.\n- "ClusterQueueStopped" means that the workload was evicted because the ClusterQueue is stopped.\n- "LocalQueueStopped" means that the workload was evicted because the LocalQueue is stopped.\n- "NodeFailures" means that the workload was evicted due to node failures when using TopologyAwareScheduling.\n- "Deactivated" means that the workload was evicted because spec.active is set to false.
